title: Practice habits and long-note exercises
summary: Hall says he did not practise long tones and finds playing a straight melody on clarinet the hardest thing.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: How long, do you still practice, like when you were learning, or in late years, I guess when you played the band every night, you wouldn't have worried about it.

No, I wasn't thinking about picking. You never think of it? The only time I used to pick up, I was interested in like, a lot of time that, when I'm playing with a small combination, just a clarinet, you know, like a rhythm session, then a lot of time, yeah, I'll run something down, I'll say, well I got to play the melody, this and that, I find out the hardest thing about the clarinet is playing the melody. That's the hardest thing to play a straight melody on the side, I think that's the hardest thing for me to do. You have to hold that long notes. Yeah, that's right, got to play just right, sure. you first learned? No. You know, you hear about those things to get a nice tone, you're supposed to practice
holding the tone and all that kind. You start that, you know, you get tired of that, you know what I mean? You want to go and do something else. Sure.
